Start after one complete [capacitance](../tutorials/capacitance.qmd) or
[resonance/EPR](../tutorials/resonance-epr.qmd) example. The next useful step is
to change one part of the model and understand which inputs and results that
change affects. Save the original model and result before preparing a new run.

## Change the source geometry

A component defines local Entity identities and authored geometry. A placed
occurrence qualifies those identities with its registered path. The final Net
assignment belongs to the assembled model: several source Entities can belong
to one electrical conductor Net without losing their individual lineage.

For a semantic component assembly, `GeometryPlan` makes those choices explicit:

```python
from scgsim.sgb import GeometryPlan

plan = GeometryPlan(
    component=component,
    root_id="chip",
    layer_stack=layer_stack,
    material_records=material_records,
    coupon_padding_um=coupon_padding_um,
)
```

Here `component`, stack, material records and padding are the actual model
inputs from your source construction. Register its actual named references
with `plan.register_instance(path, reference)`; do not register guessed paths
from flattened polygon names. Root-local Entities already belong to `chip`.
Inspect the qualified identities before assigning electrical membership:

```python
print(tuple(entity.semantic_id for entity in plan.entities))
```

Supply a mapping of final Net IDs to the exact Entity IDs from that inventory
with `plan.set_nets(net_membership)`. Choose membership from the circuit you
intend to model, including which conductors share Ground. The
[geometry reference](../geometry-sgb.qmd#component-to-backend-geometry-contract)
owns the assignment contract; the [Xmon construction](../tutorial-xmon-input.qmd)
provides a larger concrete hierarchy example.

Declare the outer vacuum envelope with `plan.set_vacuum_region(...)` and call
`plan.prepare()` to retain the source snapshot. A new geometry, material stack,
Net assignment or envelope needs a new snapshot. Changing a detached summary
dictionary does not edit the geometry that a solver will receive.

### Carry a curved source into the Palace plan

For a circular example, start from the OrPen `circular_pad_capacitor` with
`R=100 µm`, `gap=20 µm`, `die=1000 µm`, and ring inner radius `80 µm`. Keep the
stack and material definitions in OrPen; GeometryPlan consumes the component,
stack, and material records supplied by that source.

Import and construct that public source cell from the OrPen revision selected
in the [installation lesson](installation.qmd#select-the-curved-source-cell):

```python
from orpen_sc_pdk.cells import circular_pad_capacitor

component = circular_pad_capacitor(
    outer_radius_um=100.0,
    inner_radius_um=80.0,
    gap_um=20.0,
    die_side_um=1000.0,
)
```

This creates the source component; curve-aware use in the GeometryPlan flow
requires an SCGSim checkout with source-curve support.

Choose the curve description from the source you have. For authored geometry,
the component can carry `BoundaryCurveChainSpec` records in
`component.info["component_semantics"]["boundary_curves"]`, naming an existing
Entity and boundary and listing its ordered line, arc, or spline segments.
GeometryPlan qualifies those local identities for the registered occurrence
and transforms the curve chain with it. For records authored after assembly,
use `plan.set_boundary_curves(...)` with qualified IDs in assembled coordinates.
If you have only GDS boundary vertices,
select a `GdsBoundaryReconstructionSpec` in
`component.info["component_semantics"]["boundary_reconstruction"]` or pass
qualified records to `plan.set_boundary_reconstruction(...)`. Use segment and
anchor identities from the source boundary; unselected segments remain
straight. SCGSim does not infer curve intent from a preview or smooth polygon
edges implicitly.

Continue with the plan flow above: register the source's actual references,
inspect `plan.entities`, assign the intended final Net IDs with
`plan.set_nets(net_membership)`, set the vacuum region, and call
`plan.prepare()`. The snapshot retains the selected curve declarations and
their Entity and occurrence identities. Palace Routes A and B lower active
curves; Route C and AEDT planar preparation do not. With no curve declaration,
existing polygon-only behavior is unchanged.

::: {.callout-note title="Authored curves and GDS reconstruction are separate inputs"}
The two `GeometryPlan` setters replace only their caller-owned lists;
`prepare()` also adds component declarations. So
`plan.set_boundary_curves([])` does not remove OrPen-authored curves, and a GDS
reconstruction overlapping an authored full ring is rejected rather than used
as an override. To reconstruct from polygon data, create a detached raw
`GeometryBuildInput` with the selected reconstruction record and without the
authored curve declaration, then pass it to the existing public
`SemanticGeometryBuilder` API. `set_plan(snapshot)` continues to honor the
snapshot's declarations. See the
[GeometryPlan and SGB source-curve contract](../geometry-sgb.qmd#source-curves)
for curve record and boundary ownership. This does not mutate the component or
its snapshot.
:::

## Change the physical model

Ask which quantity you now need. Terminal capacitance requires terminal and
reference/ground choices. A resonant field model additionally needs the
appropriate boundaries and any explicit lumped branch. A driven response needs
ports and wave references; a line extraction needs a defined cross section.
Use [Concept](../concepts/problems.qmd) to separate those physical choices from
their backend API representation.

::: {.callout-note title="Q3D and Q2D have their own inputs"}
Q3D uses GDS imports with explicit finite-thickness layers, object/material
bindings and net/source/sink definitions. Q2D uses explicit cross-section
rectangles and conductor groups. Neither reads your GeometryPlan through a
`set_plan` method, and Q2D does not generate a slice of it.
:::

For another network question, continue to [Driven Modal](aedt-driven-modal.qmd)
or [Driven Terminal](aedt-driven-terminal.qmd). For finite conductor extraction,
use [Q3D](aedt-q3d.qmd); for per-unit-length line matrices, use [Q2D](aedt-q2d.qmd).
Their shared [CPW source example](aedt-inputs.qmd) preserves the explicit import
mapping rather than repeating it in every solver lesson.

## Change a solver request

Keep source parameters separate from native controls. Mesh size/order,
Eigenmode search target, requested number of modes, adaptation controls and
host resources answer different questions. Record the value and purpose of
each change beside the quantity you plan to inspect. Example controls in a
lesson are starting inputs, not a universal accuracy recommendation.

Prepare a new run directory and handoff for a changed request. Inspect the
[source summary](source-observations.qmd) and, when useful, the
[prepared model](solver-observations.qmd), then execute the exact new package.
Retain each result with its own settings so that a later comparison can name
which geometry, boundary and request changed.

## Decide whether a rerun is needed

| Change | Next operation |
|---|---|
| Shape, stack, Net membership or outer domain | New source snapshot/import bindings, preparation and solve |
| Boundary, terminal/port or junction circuit model | New backend model, preparation and solve |
| Mesh or native solve controls | New prepared request and solve |
| Requested field-side/margin evaluation on saved AEDT fields | Explicit [native saved-field analysis](aedt-saved-fields.qmd) if the sealed fields support it |
| Loss assumptions on an existing detached EPR result | [Offline reanalysis](offline-epr.qmd), keeping the field evidence |

Read the actual selected quantity and its available history after each run.
Keep native status and missing channels visible. The
[result-reading lesson](returned-results.qmd#interpret-for-scq-use) connects
that evidence to the engineering or physics purpose of your model.
